# ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry Daily Update (Jul 20, 2026)
## OVERVIEW 
The day saw significant progress in addressing critical issues, including the resolution of a long-standing `kona|acceptance-tests` bug and updates to `opgeth-decoupling` strategies. Documentation for super-root migration runbooks was also fixed.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

- **Automated Code Generation Update**
  An automated code generation update was initiated to keep the codebase current. This is a routine maintenance task to ensure consistency and efficiency. [#1289](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/pull/1289)

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS
- [#1289](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/pull/1289) chore: automated codegen update 2026-07-20: This pull request introduces an automated code generation update.

## CLOSED ISSUES

- **Kona Acceptance Test Resolution**
  The issue where `TestSequencerPreset` did not support the Kona sequencer was closed. It was determined that recent updates likely rendered the issue outdated. [#18675](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/18675)

- **Kona Node Syncmode Parity**
  The task to implement `syncmode.offset-el-safe` in `kona-node` for parity with `op-node` was closed. It was concluded that Kona's existing behavior already provides the safety properties this flag addresses, and implementing it would introduce a mild finalization regression. [#21243](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/21243)

- **Super-Root Migration Runbook Fixes**
  Documentation for super-root migration runbooks, specifically concerning `SUPER_PERMISSIONED` game type 5, has been fixed. [#21709](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/21709)

## NEW ISSUES
No new issues were opened today.

## ACTIVE ISSUES

- **`opgeth-decoupling`: make `op-service/sources` the OP-aware eth client** [#20264](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/20264)
  Discussion on the `op-batcher` migration strategy has evolved. It was determined that `op-batcher` cannot migrate to `InfoAndUserTxs` and will instead go payload-native. This is because `InfoAndUserTxs` drops necessary L1-info deposit transactions and post-execution transactions required for batch building. The batcher will now fetch `*eth.ExecutionPayloadEnvelope` via `PayloadByNumber`. The partitioned accessors (`InfoAndUserTxs`, `InfoAndDeposits`, `InfoAndFirstDeposit`) will still be added for test migrations. Critical considerations for receipt root derivation and transaction hash derivation were also highlighted.

- **`opgeth-decoupling`: swap call-sites to `op-core/*` across `op-node`, `op-service`, `op-batcher`** [#20263](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/20263)
  All three sub-issues related to this task are now closed. The remaining scope of this issue is being tracked in [#21901](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/21901), which covers `PostExecTx` span-batch swap and one-off fork symbols. The issue will close once [#21901](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/21901) is landed.

- **Flake: `reth-optimism-node` integration test `peers_negotiate_eth_69` SIGSEGVs on teardown** [#20973](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/20973)
  An independent review of this flake was conducted, and a candidate upstream fix was evaluated. The "detached payload thread polls a torn-down runtime" mechanism, previously suspected, was refuted by experiments. The actual mechanism of the segfault remains unidentified. The "own-runtime" patch is not being pursued as a fix because its causal claim is contradicted by experiments. The review highlighted that `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` does not affect SIGSEGVs, and local reproduction attempts are likely futile. The recommended next step is to capture a core dump/faulting stack in CI to identify the root cause. A different approach is being explored in [#21562](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/pull/21562).

- **Flaky test: `TestSupernodeLightSequencerInteropInvalidMessageReplacement`** [#21635](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/21635)
  The root cause of this recurring flake has been identified. `FollowSource` could canonicalize upstream block N+1 while the light sequencer had a timer armed against N, leading to a build start on a removed parent. This resulted in `missing parent header` and `Invalid payload attributes`, causing a critical shutdown. A draft PR ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#21913](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21913)) has been created to fix this by rejecting non-derived build starts unless their parent block ID matches the engine controller's current unsafe block ID. Verification shows the fix is effective, with regressions passing consistently.
